label: pjm 93 temp derate
definition: PJM 93 temperature-dependent derate on the pjm-90 CC_CHP SRMC recipe. Carries the pjm-90 recipe verbatim (ST_GAS overnight drag, CHP power-only HR correction, PRB/ST_CHP outage capture, CC_CHP SRMC re-grounding) and adds temp_dependent_derate=True: a physically-derived per-class dry-bulb temperature capacity curve (arXiv:2311.07001, CPUC R.21-10-002) that REPLACES the flat EIA-860 net-summer derate for CC/CT with a capacity-neutral reshape (heatwave hours below net-summer, cooler hours toward full rating) and adds a pure additive hot-hour derate for COAL/ST_GAS. RESULT: 2025 C3c scarcity tail (DA-expressible hours >$200) improved 0h->19h vs 51h actual (0.00x->0.37x, 37% of the undershoot closed, the keeper's own flagged gap); 2023 0h->2h (actual 8h) and 2024 4h->12h (actual 2h), both still small-count PASS. C1 fuel-mix (CC_REGULAR, ST_GAS) essentially unchanged -- this mechanism reshapes capacity by temperature, it does not resolve the fuel-mix volume miss (2024 ST_GAS crosses into tolerance marginally, -8.0->-7.9 TWh). No regression on any other criterion vs pjm-90: C2 system volume, C4 dispatch correlation, C5a CO2, C7 diurnal shape and C8 forced-energy all PASS; forced-energy shares and the pre-existing reliability_floor x CT_PEAKER D-4 off-window flag are unchanged. KEEPER PROMOTED 2026-07-09 (reviewed as probe 2026-07-08-pjm-93-temp-derate first, no promotion-blocking regression found), ablation twin registered (2026-07-08-pjm-93-temp-derate-ablation). Determination NOT-YET: fails C1 fuel-mix (CC_REGULAR 2023 -12.8 TWh / 2024 +11.7 TWh - volume out of band) and C3c price-tail/scarcity (2025: model 19h vs DA actual 51h >$200, 0.37x) - both pre-existing PJM model misses carried over from pjm-90, not introduced by this change; C2 system volume, C6 governance, C7 diurnal shape and C8 forced-energy all PASS.
market_story: CT_PEAKER -0.55/-1.12 TWh (2024/25): ct_netload_drag holds fast-start peakers in the evening net-load ramp, but with all floors removed the ablation lets CT clear the freed cheap energy economically -- the net cross-class delta is merit-order redistribution, not a CT-specific forced buy (same story as pjm-90). CC_REGULAR +0.34/+0.75 TWh in 2023/24 but flips to -0.35 TWh in 2025; ST_GAS +0.14/+0.08/+0.29 TWh across 2023-25: the reliability_floor overnight drag directly forces only 0.06-0.23 TWh (CC_REGULAR) / 0.21-0.28 TWh (ST_GAS) of that each year (measured CAMPD-derived commitment floor, RUC-style reliability commitment on extreme-temperature/high-net-load nights); the remainder -- including the 2025 CC_REGULAR sign flip -- is indirect economic redispatch as the floors removed elsewhere (chiefly CT_PEAKER/import) reshape the LP's clearing order, not a forced buy. COAL_BIT +2.7-4.4 TWh and import -2.6-3.6 TWh: neither class is directly floored (coal_mustrun_per_plant is unchanged between main and ablation) -- this is the system-wide merit-order echo of the floors removed on CT_PEAKER/CC_REGULAR/ST_GAS reshaping the LP's clearing order, not a forced buy. CC_CHP/CT_CHP/ST_CHP deltas <=0.15 TWh -- the offer/HR/outage corrections move level via price, not forcing.
